'''''Dimorphotheca''''' is a genus of plants in the family [[Asteraceae]], native to southern Africa.<ref>{{cite book|author=Bailey, L.H.|author2=Bailey, E.Z.| author3=Staff of the Liberty Hyde Bailey Hortorium |date=1976 |title= Hortus Third: A concise dictionary of plants cultivated in the United States and Canada |url=https://archive.org/details/hortusthirdconci00bail|url-access=registration|publisher=Macmillan |location=New York |isbn=978-0-02-505470-7 |via= archive.org}}</ref> is one of eight genera of the [[Calenduleae]], with a centre of diversity in [[Southern Africa]]. Species are native to [[Botswana]], [[Eswatini]], [[Lesotho]], [[Namibia]], [[South Africa]], and [[Zimbabwe]].<ref name = powo/> Some species can hybridize with ''[[Osteospermum]]'', and crosses are sold as cultivated ornamentals. 

The name ''Dimorphotheca'' is derived from the Greek: ''di'' (two) ''morph'' (shape) ''theka'' (receptacle), referring to the dimorphic [[cypselae]], a trait inherent to members of the Calenduleae.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://pza.sanbi.org/dimorphotheca-sinuata| title= Dimorphotheca sinuata| website= pza.sanbi.org| publisher= PlantZAfrica, South African National Biodiversity Institute | first1= Mhlonishwa D.| last1= Dlamini| first2= Roger| last2= Oliver | date= July 2002|edition= August 2020| access-date= }}</ref> Plants of this genus usually have bisexual flowers.
